entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fujiwara no Otsugu was a Japanese statesman, courtier, politician, and editor during the Heian period, playing a pivotal role in shaping the country's governance and culture. He was a key figure in the compilation of the Nihon Kōki, a foundational text of Japanese history.

As a member of the influential Fujiwara clan, Otsugu's actions had significant repercussions on the imperial court and the aristocracy. His involvement in the compilation of the Nihon Kōki helped establish a standardized narrative of Japanese history, which has been a cornerstone of the country's national identity ever since.

Otsugu's legacy extends beyond his contributions to Japanese history. His work in the imperial court paved the way for future generations of Japanese politicians and administrators, influencing the development of the samurai class and the country's feudal system.

Fujiwara no Otsugu's impact on Japanese history can be seen in the continued relevance of the Nihon Kōki, which remains a crucial source of information on the country's early history. His work serves as a testament to the enduring power of Japanese culture and the importance of understanding the country's complex and often tumultuous past.
